headline: Reformulating core sequence and graph primitives to run at pangenome and read-mapping…
label: Scalable Genomic Analysis Tools
summary: Terabase-scale pangenome analysis and paired-end short-read mapping require primitives that remain tractable as collection and read-set sizes grow.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reformulating a core primitive so that its cost becomes tractable at scale, achieved through changes in representation or decomposition rather than a single shared mechanism. The RLBWT-based work computes LCP arrays in compressed space with O(r) space and optimal time for repetitive collections, targeting terabase-scale pangenome analysis. GenPairX co-designs hardware and algorithm, using a joint pair filter and lightweight alignment for paired-end short-read mapping. VAT provides a unified, extensible alignment framework built on multi-view indexing and bitonic-sort radix clustering. gLeiden implements Leiden community detection on GPUs with directed-graph support and reports speedups over Java and cuGraph. The items do not converge on one architecture or method, and the evidence is predominantly preprint, with gLeiden the only published item.
